title: PropertiesPanel frame view: show/edit frame label, tween ease, and tweenType when no object is selected
description:
## Problem

In Flash 8, the Properties panel is context-sensitive. When no display object is selected, it shows the **Frame** view, which contains:

- Frame label (text input) and label type (name / comment / anchor dropdown)
- Tween type selector (None / Motion / Shape)
- Ease slider (−100..100) and custom ease button (opens EaseCurveDialog)
- Rotate mode dropdown (None / Auto / CW / CCW) and count field
- Sound selector (for per-frame sound attachments)

Currently the authoring UI has **no frame view** in PropertiesPanel. `PanelView` (PropertiesPanel.tsx line 70) has `"document" | "shape" | "instance" | "text" | "mixed"` — no `"frame"`. When nothing is selected, the panel shows the document-level view (stage size, FPS, background color). Frame labels can only be set via the JSFL runtime or the agent MCP tools.

## What to implement

### 1. Add a `FrameView` component to PropertiesPanel

Create a `FrameView` sub-component (or inline it in `PropertiesPanel`) that is shown when `selectedObjects.length === 0` AND a keyframe (or a frame within a tween) is active.

The frame view should expose:

**Label section**
- Text input for `frame.label` (updates on blur / Enter)
- Dropdown for `frame.labelType` (`"name"` | `"comment"` | `"anchor"`)

**Tween section** (shown only when the active frame is a keyframe)
- Radio or dropdown: Tween = None / Motion / Shape
- When Motion is selected: Ease slider (−100..100) + "Custom ease…" button that opens the existing `EaseCurveDialog`
- Rotate mode (None / Auto / CW / CCW) + count field
- "Orient to path" checkbox (when a guide layer is above)

**Sound section** (when Motion = None or frame is a normal keyframe)
- Sound dropdown (lists SoundItems from the library) — delegates to the existing `SoundPanel`; can be a simplified re-use or pointer to SoundPanel

### 2. Wire the FrameView to Shell

- Pass the current governing `Frame` (and its tween span, if any) as a prop to `PropertiesPanel`.
- Add an `onFrameUpdate(updates: Partial<Frame>)` callback to `PropertiesPanel` props, implemented in Shell using the existing `setFrameScript`, `setMotionTween`, `setFrameLabel`, etc. model functions.
- When a custom ease is confirmed via `EaseCurveDialog`, call `setMotionTween(..., easeCurve)`.

### 3. Switch PropertiesPanel view to "frame" when nothing selected

```ts
type PanelView = "document" | "frame" | "shape" | "instance" | "text" | "mixed";
function getPanelView(selectedObjects, activeFrame): PanelView {
  if (selectedObjects.length === 0) return activeFrame ? "frame" : "document";
  // ...existing logic...
}
```

Show the document view only when there is no active frame (e.g., the document has no layers or the timeline is empty).

## Acceptance criteria

- Selecting nothing while on frame 0 (a keyframe) shows Frame properties in the Properties panel, not document properties.
- Editing the label input and pressing Enter sets `frame.label` on the active keyframe (visible in the Timeline as a flag on that keyframe).
- Changing the Tween dropdown from None → Motion creates a motion tween (same as right-clicking in the Timeline).
- Moving the Ease slider from 0 to 50 changes `frame.motionEase` to 50.
- Clicking "Custom ease…" opens the EaseCurveDialog; confirming a curve sets `frame.motionEaseCurve`.
- The document properties view is still accessible (e.g., when clicking an empty area outside the timeline, or via Modify > Document).
